html:
At Aljubarrota, on 14 August 1385, a Portuguese army with English archers defeated a much larger army of Castile and its French allies. It saved Portugal's independence.

When King Ferdinand I died in 1383 without a son, the king of Castile, married to his daughter, claimed the crown. Many Portuguese, especially in Lisbon, backed João of Aviz, a half-brother of the late king, who was proclaimed King John I. His general Nuno Álvares Pereira chose a strong position and his men beat off the Castilian charges.

The victory founded the House of Aviz, which led Portugal into the age of discovery. In thanks King John built the great monastery of Batalha nearby. The English alliance was sealed soon after. His sons led the conquest of Ceuta in 1415.
